'''Kwaku Aning''' (born in 1946)<ref name=":Repr"/> is a [[Ghana]]ian [[diplomat]],scientist, engineer, international civil servant and technologist who was [[Chairman]] of the governing board of the [[Ghana Atomic Energy Commission]], having been appointed in July 2017. Aning is a former Deputy Director-General of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]]. and prior to that the Secretary of the Policy Making Organs of the IAEA 2000-2010 <ref name=":Repr">{{cite press release|url=https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/new-representative-iaea-director-general-united-nations|title=New Representative of the IAEA Director General to the United Nations|publisher=International Atomic Energy Agency|date=15 February 2000|access-date=25 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=18 Jan 2005 |title=DG of International Atomic Energy Agency to visit Ghana |publisher=GhanaWeb |url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/DG-of-International-Atomic-Energy-Agency-to-visit-Ghana-73670}}</ref>
 
As Deputy Director General, he was head of the Department of Technical Cooperation at the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]], an [[international agency]] under the auspices of the [[United Nations]]. He took up his position on January 1, 2010, and ended in June, 2015.<ref name="IAEA1">{{cite web |title=IAEA Management Team |url=http://www.iaea.org/About/dg/aning_bio.html |access-date=17 July 2013 |publisher=IAEA}}</ref><ref name="IAEA2">{{cite web |last=Valdre |first=Pim |date=28 February 2012 |title=Interview with Dr. Kwaku Aning, International Atomic Energy Agency |url=http://www.theglobalobservatory.org/interviews/227-interview-with-dr-kwaku-aning-international-atomic-energy-agency.html |access-date=17 July 2013 |website= |publisher=[[International Peace Institute]]}}</ref>

Prior to his appointment as Deputy Director-General, he served as the Director and Secretary of the Policy Making Organs of the IAEA. He has also been the Representative of the IAEA Director General to the [[United Nations]]. He is a member of the board of trustees of [[Kuwait]]'s Al-Sumait Prize for African Development.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnbcafrica.com/apo/2017/12/14/the-winner-of-kuwaits-alsumait-prize-for-african-development-for-2017-in-the-field-of-education-today-received-their-award-at-a-special-ceremony-held-in-kuwait-city/|title=The winner of Kuwait's Al-Sumait Prize for African Development for 2017 in the field of Education today received their award at a special ceremony held in Kuwait City - CNBC Africa|date=2017-12-14|work=CNBC Africa|access-date=2018-04-22|language=en-US}}</ref> 
 
In September 2015, Aning became a Governor of [[IAEA Board of Governors]] and still serves in this position.

==Early life and education== 
Aning was born in 1946 in [[Ghana]]. He was educated at [[Accra Academy]] and Mfantsipim Secondary School. Aning completed a bachelor's degree in [[mechanical engineering]] in 1968 from the [[Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology|University of Science and Technology]], graduating with first class honours, as one of the first four persons to obtain first class honours in the Engineering Sciences from the university.<ref name="Accra Aca Is Calling">{{cite web |title=Accra Aca Is Calling and Mfantsipim Secondary School|url=http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/features/artikel.php?ID=116583&comment=2517532 |access-date=30 May 2008 |publisher=GhanaWeb}}</ref> That same year, he entered [[Princeton University]] receiving a master's degree in [[Solid State Physics]] in 1971. Aning obtained a doctoral degree in [[metallurgical engineering]] from [[Columbia University]] in 1976.<ref name=":Ghanaian">{{Cite news |author=Ghana News Agency |title=Ghanaian gets maiden African appointment at IAEA |publisher=Ghana Dot. |url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Appreciate-research-value-for-quality-healthcare-delivery-Dr-Aning-654321}}</ref>

==Career==
Aning started his working career as a Technical Advisor to the UN Conference on Science and Technology for Development. In January 1980, Aning became a Senior Scientific Affairs Officer of the [[United Nations|UN]] Centre for Science and Technology, remaining in this position for the next twelve years. He worked in this role which had a special focus on science and technology development of developing countries. Aning moved on to the [[United Nations Peacekeeping Operations|UN Peacekeeping Department]], working as a Regional Election Officer for the period between March 1992 to June 1994 . Aning was made a Senior Officer, [[United Nations Secretariat|Office of the Secretary-General]] later on within August 1998 and January 2000.

In February 2000, Kwaku Aning joined the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] as the Representative of the Director General of the agency to the United Nations in [[New York City|New York]].<ref name=":Repr"/><ref name="IAEA1"/>

Aning was the Chairman of the Nuclear Power Institute, GAEC. Aning was also Chairman of the Governing Board, [[Ghana Atomic Energy Commission]].<ref>{{cite web |date=21 May 2018 |title=Nuclear Power prospects bright- Ghanaian engineers push for support |url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Nuclear-power-prospects-bright-Ghanaian-engineers-push-for-support-653516 |publisher=GhanaWeb.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=23 May 2018 |title=Appreciate research value for quality healthcare - Dr.Aning |publisher=GhanaWeb. |url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Appreciate-research-value-for-quality-healthcare-delivery-Dr-Aning-654321}}</ref>

==Family and personal life==
Aning married Arafua Apaloo-Aning, a political activist and keen gardener<ref>{{Cite news|title=How two dynamic women are helping to green Ghana|url=https://thebftonline.com/archive/more.php?ID=3560|location=Accra, Ghana|newspaper=[[Business and Financial Times]]}}{{Dead link|date=May 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
